newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Pacific Rim investing at a distance.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Pacific Rim investing at a distance.

text.p: Roy Papp, co-portfolio manager of the new Papp America-Pacific Rim Fund, is bullish on the Pacific region -- but from a distance.
Papp said the fund, which was launched on March 14, will invest only a small portion of the fund in companies headquartered in the Pacific Rim.
The bulk of the portfolio will be in U.S. companies that earn a large proportion their revenues in the region, especially growth companies.
"We're interested in companies that derive at least 30 percent of their sales or earnings from the Pacific Rim," including Japan, said Papp. "The average is 31 percent."

The fund is shying away from local companies due to the illiquidity of trading on local exchanges and because accounting practices of local firms are not as stringent as those in the United States or Europe.
"We love the region," Papp said, noting that China and Hong Kong offer good growth prospects. Thailand, he said, offered "a wonderful opportunity but volatile as hell."
The fund has bulked up on such global giants as Intel Corp and L.M. Ericsson, which he estimates each derive about 33 percent of revenues from the region; and General Electric Co.
Other multinational holdings, with big presences in the region are ad agency giant Interpublic Group.
One local holding is Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd. Another is Bancorp Hawaii.
It's not a new idea for Papp. His America-Abroad fund is a who's who of large-cap multinational growth stocks.

While the Pacific Rim fund is a month old, a spokesman for Morningstar Inc said the fund has not yet been assigned to a sector, but will likely be classified as large cap domestic growth fund since it's not really participating directly in the region.
The prospectus said it "may invest a maximum of 30 percent of its...assets in common stocks of foreign-domiciled companies that are either traded directly or as ADRs" in U.S. exchanges.

According to Morningstar, the top performing funds in that sector for the last 12 months are Rydex OTC fund which returned 31.84 percent, Buffalo U.S. Global, up 29.87 percent; Reynolds Blue Chip Growth, up 27.53 percent; and Deyfus Appreciation, which rose 22.92 percent.
Papp said he plans to keep no more than two to three percent in cash, and run a slim portfolio of about 25 issues.
